definitions.explanation: Extremely small in size, scale, or detail. Used for particles, structures, differences, and other things that are difficult to perceive with the naked eye or require close examination.

examples.japanese: {微細|びさい}な{粒子|りゅうし}。
{微細|びさい}な{違|ちが}いを{見分|みわ}ける。
{顕微鏡|けんびきょう}でしか{見|み}えないほど{微細|びさい}な{構造|こうぞう}が、{生命|せいめい}の{仕組|しく}みを{支|ささ}えている。
examples.english: Microscopic structures invisible to the naked eye support the mechanisms of life.

notes:
FORMS:
- Modifier: {微細|びさい}な
- Adverbial: {微細|びさい}に

USAGE:
{微細|びさい} is a formal, often technical or scientific word. It is frequently used in academic writing, manufacturing, and medicine to describe extremely small scales.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {微細|びさい}な{粒子|りゅうし}: fine particles
- {微細|びさい}な{構造|こうぞう}: fine structure, microstructure
- {微細|びさい}な{変化|へんか}: minute changes
- {微細|びさい}{加工|かこう}: microfabrication, micro-processing

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {微細|びさい}: minute, microscopic (technical, scientific)
- {細|こま}かい: fine, detailed (everyday)
- {微小|びしょう}: tiny, minuscule (emphasizes smallness)
- {精密|せいみつ}: precise, fine (emphasizes precision)
